head: 3bbbe50ed471d88a8c351df5a7340208ea9e736f
guard_text: - No direct `EntityManagerInterface` in services/handlers — use repository interfaces
ablate: - No direct `EntityManagerInterface` in services/handlers — use repository interfaces
task_source: constructed: no recent commit in the persistence-layer area has an un-done analogue at HEAD; the task fixes a real gap at HEAD (DeleteSourceController calls sourceRepository->remove() but article.source_id, user_article_read/user_article_bookmark/notification_log.article_id FKs have no ON DELETE CASCADE, so deleting a source that has articles fails).
task: Deleting a source from the Sources page currently fails with a foreign-key error whenever the source already has articles, because nothing removes the articles (and the read states, bookmarks and notification logs that reference them) first. Fix source deletion so that removing a source also deletes all of its articles and every row that depends on those articles, then the source itself. Put the deletion logic in a dedicated service in the Source module (with an interface, like the other services) so it can be reused later, and have DeleteSourceController use it. Keep the existing HTMX and flash-message behaviour of the controller unchanged.
default_behaviour: Inject Doctrine\ORM\EntityManagerInterface into the new SourceDeletionService (or the controller) and run DQL/QueryBuilder deletes or persist/remove/flush directly, instead of adding deleteBySource/removeByArticles methods to Article/UserArticleRead/UserArticleBookmark/NotificationLog repository interfaces.

evidence.how_counted: follow: PHP files under src/ outside */Repository/ that inject a *RepositoryInterface constructor dependency (grep -rlE 'RepositoryInterface \$' src | grep -v /Repository/ = 56), including DeleteSourceController (SourceRepositoryInterface->remove) and ToggleBookmarkController (bookmarkRepository->remove). contra: files outside */Repository/ referencing EntityManager/ObjectManager/ManagerRegistry = 0. Not counted as contra but adjacent: 4 files use Doctrine\DBAL\Connection directly (CleanupCommand does raw DELETEs on article/user_article_read/notification_log; QueueDepthService; ConversationMessageStore; HealthController).

cell_reason: Every service, handler and controller in src—including DeleteSourceController the task edits—persists through repository interfaces and none injects an EntityManager, though no comment explains why.
check_cmd: { git diff HEAD -U0 -- src | awk '/^\+\+\+ /{f=$2; next} /^\+/{ if (f !~ /\/Repository\//) print }'; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- src | grep -v '/Repository/' | while read -r f; do cat "$f"; done; } | grep -Eq 'EntityManagerInterface|EntityManager\b|ObjectManager|ManagerRegistry|getManager(ForClass)?\(' && echo VIOLATED || echo OBEYED
violation_example: Created src/Source/Service/SourceDeletionService.php with `use Doctrine\ORM\EntityManagerInterface;` and constructor `private EntityManagerInterface $em` -> VIOLATED; separately added `private readonly \Doctrine\ORM\EntityManagerInterface $em,` to DeleteSourceController constructor -> VIOLATED; adding 'EntityManager' text inside src/Source/Repository/SourceRepository.php -> OBEYED (repository implementations are allowed).
notes: Check flags EntityManagerInterface/EntityManager/ObjectManager/ManagerRegistry/getManager( in added lines of src files outside */Repository/ and in untracked src files outside */Repository/; repositories may legitimately use the EM. It counts a controller injection as violation although the rule names services/handlers (Symfony controllers are services here). Raw DBAL Connection use (as CleanupCommand does) is not flagged since the rule names EntityManagerInterface; an agent mimicking CleanupCommand would bypass repositories without registering as a violation. Alternative valid solution: a migration adding ON DELETE CASCADE—obeys the rule. docs/todo/architecture-audit.md is stale and claims '30+ direct EntityManager usages', which could mislead an agent that reads it. CLAUDE.md also says 'Interface-first: all service and repository boundaries defined by interface' (kept, not ablated) which partially implies the practice.
